help.title: Help

stepHints.listener: The app could not reach its own proxy. Try quitting and opening it again.
stepHints.dns: The secure lookup failed. Try another secure-DNS server in Settings, Advanced.
stepHints.youtube: YouTube did not answer through the app. Tap Fix connection below.
stepHints.video: Video servers did not answer. Tap Fix connection below.

help.testNothingWorked: None of the methods worked on this connection. Your network may be blocking the secure lookup. Open Settings, Advanced, and try another secure-DNS server.

problems.a1: Run the connection test. If a step fails, tap Fix connection. Then fully close your browser and open it again.
problems.a2: Younblock keeps running in the tray, near the clock. Click its icon to open the window. Choose Quit to stop it completely.
problems.q3: Does it work in other browsers or apps?
problems.a3: It sets the Windows proxy, so every mainstream browser works — Edge, Chrome, Firefox, Opera, Brave and the rest. It is tested most with Chrome. Apps that ignore Windows' proxy setting won't use it.
problems.q4: My internet stopped after the app closed.
problems.a4: Tap "Restore internet settings" below. It removes the setting the app added. It also happens automatically the next time the app starts.
problems.q5: Windows or my antivirus shows a warning.
problems.a5: The app is not code-signed yet, and Windows warns about unsigned apps that change proxy settings. Only run it from a source you trust.
problems.a6: No. It does not hide your IP address and adds no encryption; YouTube's own HTTPS still protects the content. It only changes how the first message to the site is sent.
problems.a7: Tap Fix connection once. If it still buffers, the limit is probably your connection speed, not this app.

about.title: About
how: Your browser sends its request to Younblock, which runs only on your PC.
Younblock looks up YouTube's address with a secure DNS service, so the lookup can't be tampered with on the way.
Younblock sends the first "hello" message to YouTube in small pieces. Filters that scan that message for the website's name usually don't recognise the pieces.
After that, everything flows normally, protected by YouTube's own HTTPS.
not: It does not hide your IP address.
It does not add encryption beyond what HTTPS already provides.
Your internet provider can still see which servers you connect to.
It may stop working if the filtering changes.
privacy: No account, no analytics, no updates in the background.
The only network requests are secure DNS lookups to the provider in use and the YouTube checks the app runs.
Website names are not written to the log unless you turn that on.
